fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says, "Son of man, these men have set up idols in their hearts…" (Ezekiel 14:3). Son of man is the name the LORD uses when He speaks to Ezekiel. The text puts the idols right there, in their hearts.

I get the guess, friend. Idols and houses go together in most people's heads. But the LORD says the idols are set up "…in their hearts…" (Ezekiel 14:3). He is speaking to Ezekiel, and the verse names the elders' hearts, not their homes.

Hilltops are a fair guess, friend. Not here, though. The LORD tells Ezekiel these men "…have set up idols in their hearts…" (Ezekiel 14:3). Nobody had to climb anything. The whole problem was sitting inside them.

Close, but the text says otherwise, friend. The LORD does ask Ezekiel: "Should I consult with them in any way?" (Ezekiel 14:3). He says it about the elders who had come and sat down. So the question is really in there, right after He describes their idols and stumbling blocks.

Easy one to reach for, friend. Still, the verse never gives exile as the reason. The LORD says He will answer "…so that I may take hold of the hearts of the people of Israel." (Ezekiel 14:5). The reason is about their hearts.

I love the energy, friend, but that's not the word. The LORD says, "Repent and turn away from your idols…" (Ezekiel 14:6). Rejoicing is wonderful, but the first step here is turning around. Think of a wrong turn: before anything else, you turn the car around.

Remembering is a fine thing, baker, and Scripture talks about it a lot. But in this verse the LORD says, "Repent and turn away from your idols…" (Ezekiel 14:6). He tells them to turn away from their idols, not just to think about them. The word is Repent.

The elders are the ones sitting before Ezekiel, so I get it, friend. But the LORD says who enticed the prophet: "…then it was I the LORD who enticed him…" (Ezekiel 14:9). The verse names the LORD, not the elders. It's a heavy one, and the text doesn't say more about how.

Good thinking, baker, but this verse doesn't say that. The LORD says, "But if the prophet is enticed to speak a message, then it was I the LORD who enticed him…" (Ezekiel 14:9). He names Himself as the one.

That's a fair thought, baker, but this verse says something else. The LORD says, "…I will stretch out My hand against him and destroy him from among My people Israel." (Ezekiel 14:9). It's a hard one.

Not quite, friend, it's the opposite. The LORD says it is "…in order that the house of Israel may no longer stray from Me…" (Ezekiel 14:11). He wants them to stop straying, not to stay far. After all the hard words, this verse points back toward Him.
